title: Factorization conjecture for concentrated homogeneous polynomials
statement:
Let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be independent and uniformly chosen from $\{-1,1\}$, and let

$$
f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=\sum_{1\leq i_1\dots\leq i_k}a_{i_1\dots i_k}x_{i_1}\dots x_{i_k}
$$

be a degree-$k$ homogeneous polynomial with at least $mn^{k-1}$ nonzero coefficients. **Polynomial factorization conjecture.** If the concentration satisfies

$$
\sup_c\mathbb{P}(f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=c)=\Omega_k(m^{-k/2+\epsilon}),
$$

then $f$ differs in only a few coefficients from a polynomial which factors. The same passage also conjectures the upper bound $\sup_c\mathbb{P}(f(x_1,\dots,x_n)=c)=O(m^{-1/2})$ under the stated coefficient-count hypothesis.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2009). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0704.2953](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.2953).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.1538

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2009).
source_name: Kevin P. Costello, “Bilinear and Quadratic Variants on the Littlewood-Offord Problem”, arXiv:0902.1538 (2009).
